chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered upon a man from the Ansar, and behold, there was a female slave who was heavily pregnant and moving. He asked about her, and he said: 'I bought her, O Messenger of Allah, and she is with this pregnancy.' He said: 'Did you have intercourse with her?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Free what is in her womb.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and by what does it earn manumission?' He said: 'Because your seed nourished its hearing, its sight, its flesh, and its blood.'

key_terms.أَعْتِقْ مَا فِي بَطْنِهَا: Free what is in her womb
key_terms.أَقَرَبْتَهَا: Did you have intercourse with her?

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a fetus if the master has intercourse with its pregnant slave mother?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *lhuq* (attachment of the child to the father) through the specific mechanism of the master's seed nourishing the fetus, thereby granting it the right to manumission upon the master's death or voluntary act. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the physical connection via semen creates a direct lineage and emancipation status, distinct from mere gestation. The ruling underscores the spiritual and physical value of the progeny within the household structure.
